subject: Truncated parameters with truncation defined by min of other parameters

messages.author: f4333045fa3bd674
messages.subject: Truncated parameters with truncation defined by min of other parameters
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to sample from a vector of parameters from a distribution such that the i-th parameter's prior is truncated above by the min of a subset of the previous parameters (the subset index vector is fixed for each i) and I am getting this error 

Defining model Error in topological.sort(graph, mode = "out") : At core/properties/dag.c:114 : The graph has cycles; topological sorting is only possible in acyclic graphs, Invalid value

I believe (but certainly could be wrong) the issue has to do with the fact that I am using the minimum to define the bound and that forces nimble to try to redefine the dependence structure of the model at every iteration. I've tried a few different alternatives and nothing has resolved the issue. My priors are calculated as follows inside of the nimbleCode block:

for(j in 1:k){
    if(has_dep_vec[j]==1){ #does the parameter depend on previous?
      prev.pars <- pars[1:(i-1)]
      ub <- get_bound(i,inherit.mat[1:k,1:k],prev.pars)
      pars[j] ~ T(dt(mu=0, tau=1,df=1),0,ub)
      } else {
        pars[j] ~ dt(mu=0, tau=1,df=1)
        }
  }

where the get_bound function is given by:

get_bound <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(i = double(0),
                 inherit_mat = double(2),
                 pars_prev = double(1)){
    returnType(double(0))
   
    lb <- Inf
    test <- FALSE
    j <- 1
    for(r in 1:(i-1)){
      test <- inherit_mat[r,i]>0
      if(test){
        lb <- min(lb,pars_prev[r])
      }
    }
    return(lb)   
  }
)

for k=4, inherit.mat could look like this:

inherit.mat = matrix(c(rep(0,8),
                                              0,1,0,0,
                                              1,1,0,0),
                                            ncol=4,nrow=4)

but in general inherit mat will always have the upper triangle (including the diagonal filled with 0's).

Any help will be sincerely appreciated!

Daniel

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Truncated parameters with truncation defined by min of other parameters
parts:
Hi Daniel,

A couple reactions:

1) In `pars[1:(i-1)]`, do you mean to have `j` rather than `i`?
2) You can't use `if` in model code in the way you're using it. Please see here for how `if` can only be used to define alternative model structures from the same code block. That is the only
allowable use of `if` in model code.

In terms of where to go, I think you could do this with `dconstraint` by setting up a constraint for each element of `pars`. Given your subset is fixed, I think that should be reasonably
straightforward. You might also be able to use `dinterval`. Both are described in some detail in the manual.

You could write out the individual dconstraint statements "manually" if the length of `pars` is not too big. Or something like this might work less manually:

for(j in 1:k)
  pars[j] ~ dconstraint(bound_fun(j, pars[1:(j-1)], inherit.mat))

where `bound_fun` would be essentially the same as `get_bound` presumably.

Make sure you only pass in the previous `pars` elements or else our graph processing will detect a cycle.

-chris

That i-1 index should be j-1, and I had no idea I could not use the if/else in the model code. I replaced things as you suggested and worked like a charm.

Thank you so much for looking into it so promptly, and happy holidays!! 

Daniel
